correctness.rationale: Every polynomial in scope is positive at integers; its reduction has exactly two simple roots modulo each odd prime. The three shifts in each root residue have pairwise p-adic separation exactly p^(-s), with distinct child residues 0,1,2 modulo p, giving a complete and disjoint cylinder partition. The triple moment follows from the criterion that the second-largest of three divisibility depths is at most s; geometric summation proves the rational third cumulant. Its first depth is negative only at p=3, and its strict positive depth increment proves the complete sign law; pairwise covariances are strictly positive. Independently direct integer evaluation matched all cells in 400 complete prime-power histograms, totaling 1,396,368 index triples. Uniform polynomial growth and geometric valuation tails justify empirical moment convergence.

originality.rationale: The claim is the full trivariate valuation distribution at three equispaced prime-power shifts and the sign of its connected third cumulant. Existing source-level individual polynomial valuation trees and known general bivariate simple-root valuation laws cover all marginal and pairwise facts, but do not imply the trivariate distribution or its sign-exception classification. Fully inspected relevant primary sources and targeted scientific searches revealed no dominating trivariate statement. A more general unindexed local-zeta or multivariate root-ball theorem remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent three-point result may exist in unindexed higher-order p-adic local zeta or polynomial correlation literature.

The three-shift case is a specialization of general root-ball intersection methods; originality is in the explicit complete triple law, third connected cumulant and sharp sign transition, not Hensel lifting or pairwise facts.

value.rationale: Three-point connected dependence is a motivated arithmetic statistic which cannot be recovered from pairwise joint valuations. Its unexpectedly negative value at only the smallest ternary separation, despite every pair remaining positively correlated, identifies a sharp characteristic-dependent collective obstruction caused by three roots occupying all three child cylinders. The full trivariate distribution and exact all-depth prime-power census make this an infinite structural classification, not a re-labeling of a two-point result.
